page: Amazon Web Services r8idn.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel processors capable of reaching clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz. The instance provisions 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, combined with 128.0 GB of system memory, delivering a ratio of 8.0 GB of memory per vCPU.

For workloads demanding low-latency temporary storage, the r8idn.4xlarge includes 950 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The platform features a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps, supporting significant data throughput. It operates without hardware GPU accelerators and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the r8idn.4xlarge packages dedicated high-frequency compute, high memory density, and bundled fast NVMe storage into a single deployment unit. This design reduces dependencies on separate network-attached storage for intermediate caching, making it efficient for transactional and high-memory workloads. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, relational database engines, and real-time big data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r8idn.4xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance configured on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. By unifying high memory capacity, dedicated high-frequency compute, and low-latency local storage, the instance eliminates the operational overhead of external block volumes for scratch space and temporary caching. This resource configuration is designed for memory-intensive workloads including in-memory databases, large-scale caching clusters, data analytics engines, and transactional database systems requiring consistent high-throughput network and I/O performance.
